title: Double bass
summary: Four open strings (E1, A1, D2, G2) and three stopped notes. D3 is bowed at 0.1286 of its sounding length and locks to one slip per period at the bow's centre (its third bow port still slips twice); it sounds 6.9 cents sharp of equal temperament. Eb2, stopped on the A string with 512 body modes and the bass's own bow-hair row, sounds 7.1 cents sharp of equal temperament and locks to one slip per period at the bow's centre in 69 of 74 periods. Db4, stopped on the D string with 512 body modes, the bass's own bow-hair row and the bow at one eleventh of the sounding length, sounds its note 14.0 cents sharp of equal temperament, and its bow no longer locks: the centre cell slips once in 107 of 265 periods, twice in 140 and three times in 18, where the page with the violin row slipped once in 263 of 264. A1, D2 and G2 at 512 modes carry the bass's own row too, and their centre cell slips four or five times (A1, where the 256-mode page locked to one), two to four times (D2) and two to five times (G2) per period. The body is a computed shell. A1, D2, G2, Eb2 and Db4 keep its lowest 512 modes, to about 2.88 kHz, the other pages 256, to 1623.5 Hz: above the last mode it neither moves nor radiates, so the pages are much darker than the recordings from about 3 kHz up. It is spruce and maple shell with a 116 L air cavity through the f-holes, from Johannsson's printed bass dimensions on the cello shell route, not a scan; wood below 150 Hz is a declared extrapolation. The bow is a 10 mm ribbon (16 mm, the bass's own row, on A1, Eb2, Db4, D2 and G2; E1 and D3 keep the violin row) with hair compliance on the measured rosin curve (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025, eq. 13). The after-length is a sixth of the speaking length or a sixth x 116/115, a ratio borrowed from the cello.
physics_present: computed double-bass shell body: spruce top and bass bar, maple back, ribs and bridge, from Johannsson's printed bass dimensions on the cello shell route; A1, D2, G2, Eb2 and Db4 keep the lowest 512 modes, ending at about 2.88 kHz, the other pages 256, ending at 1623.5 Hz; first structural mode 106 Hz
air cavity of 116 L breathing through the f-holes (a physical neck); coupled air mode 61 Hz
wood from the measured spruce (from 100 Hz) and maple (from 150 Hz) packs, with the lower band edge moved to 90 Hz as a declared extrapolation, not a measurement
Thomastik Spirocore Orchestra 4/4 medium strings (maker's tension table, line mass and gauges) at a 1.100 m speaking length, bending modes in two polarisations, with a bending stiffness

bow of finite width: a 10 mm ribbon of 3 cells with hair compliance (Pitteroff and Woodhouse 1998); on A1, Eb2, Db4, D2 and G2 the bass's own row, a 16 mm ribbon with 127 hairs in contact over 0.53 m, which gives the S 1.9e5 N/m and D 31 kg/s they print for a bass bow; E1 and D3 carry the violin row (S 6.1e4 N/m, D 10 kg/s)
friction law measured on real rosin (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025, eq. 13), a steady sliding curve
static compliance of the omitted body modes at the bridge and under the bow (exact static Green)
after-length (bridge to tailpiece): one sixth of the speaking length (E1) or one sixth x 116/115 (A1, D2, G2), the printed bowed-string rule with the cello's 116 mm ratio borrowed
a bow gesture on a fixed schedule: a 0.15 s ramp to the note's force at 0.15 m/s, then a 20 ms lift; each page states its bow force

a finger stop on the stopped notes (D3, Eb2): a normal contact on the string at the equal-tempered station; its limit (1000 N on D3 and Eb2) is the solver's guard, not a finger's force, and no print gives a finger force
physics_missing: body modes above the 512th on A1, D2, G2, Eb2 and Db4 and the 256th on the other pages: above about 2.88 kHz or 1623.5 Hz the body neither moves nor radiates, and the pages are much darker than the recordings from about 3 kHz up. D2 reads 10 of 14 at 512 modes with the bass row against 12 at 256, mostly because the grader reads a shorter sustain on that clip

stopped notes: D3 sits 14 cents sharp of its recording, and its bow locks only at the centre, the third port slipping twice in most periods; Eb2 sits within 0.5 cents of its recording, but its fourth harmonic is 23 dB under the recording's and its second and third 7 dB over; with four changes at once (512 modes, the bass hair row, the 1000 N guard and a raised-limit binary) this render cannot say which let it finish; Db4 sits 24.9 cents sharp of its recording (which is 10.9 cents flat of equal temperament), its harmonics above the first are 12 to 28 dB under the recording's from H2 to H5, so the centroid is 305 Hz against 789 Hz, and with the bass row its bow no longer locks and its attack reads 94 ms against the recording's 5 ms

the bass bow-hair row (Pitteroff and Woodhouse 1998, S 1.9e5 N/m, D 31 kg/s) did not raise the grade on A1, Db4, D2 or G2, against the same card with the violin row graded the same way: A1 13 of 14 against 13 (strict 13 against 13), its centre cell slipping four or five times per period where the 256-mode page locked (the 512-mode page it ties was never traced); Db4 6 of 14 against 6 (strict 6 against 5) with its lock gone, its attack at 94 ms against 11 ms and its fundamental 24.9 cents from the recording's against 21.8; D2 10 against 10 (strict 9 against 10: the third-octave envelope moves in, the wavelet spectrum out); G2 12 against 12 (strict 12 against 12). Eb2 reads 12 against 10, with four changes at once as stated above. A1, D2, G2 and Db4 do not lock with the bass row; Eb2 locks in 69 of 74 periods

pages with the bass row that did not post: E1 at 512 modes graded 5 of 14 against 6 and D3 6 against 8, each losing the lock it had (E1 slips once in 7 of 39 periods, D3 three to five times in 140), so both stay on the violin row

the melody's C3 at 512 modes with the bass row (0.6 s) was refused by the engine 0.358 s in, all three ribbon cells sticking: modal contact residual 2.61e-10 N exceeds 2.16e-10 N after 821 iterations; the melody stays on the violin row

a measured bass: the body is mapped from a maker's published specification onto the il Cannone specimen tables, not scanned; the bass bar is moved 18.1 mm inward to clear the f-hole (no source prints that position); the bridge is a uniform 152.6 g shell; the 1.070 m of a 3/4 instrument is not modelled
measured wood properties below 150 Hz (maple) and 100 Hz (spruce)
string loss: none is printed for these strings, so the cards carry none and the notes ring on after the bow lifts
string torsion: the cards carry no twist modes
the rosin's temperature and contact history: the friction is a steady sliding curve with no thermal or third-body memory
a printed double-bass after-length: the 116/115 ratio is borrowed from the cello
player variation: bow speed and force follow a fixed schedule
blocked: the melody's C3 on the bass row (refused 0.358 s in by the modal contact residual).
